item.title: Make listItems follow cursor pagination
item.brief: In inventory-client, change listItems(transport) so it resolves to every item in order by following next_cursor until it is null or absent. The first request sends no cursor; each later request passes the previous next_cursor back unchanged. Add tests with a fake transport covering multiple pages, a single page, and a missing next_cursor. Update the README to document the paginated behaviour. Run npm test and make sure it passes. Commit the change. Follow the shared contract exactly.

agt_01M89ZQVRY33N3QBNHJT48BAME:1.description: Repeated-cursor check only compares next_cursor with the immediately previous cursor, so a multi-cursor cycle (A→B→A) is not detected and listItems loops forever, growing items without bound. Reproduced: 1001+ requests with no error. Fix: track all seen cursors in a Set and reject any repeat; add a test for a two-cursor cycle. at client.js:25

agt_01M89ZQVRY33N3QBNHJT48BAME:2.description: The repeated-cursor test only covers a self-loop (next_cursor equal to the current cursor), so the multi-cursor cycle bug is not caught. at test/client.test.js:58

agt_01M89ZQVRY33N3QBNHJT48BAME:3.description: README documents the stop and non-200 rejection but not the rejections for a page without an items array or a repeated cursor, which the code now enforces. at README.md:6

agt_01M89ZS3GZ6X2X2V0FYNV6S2KV:2.description: On the base client.js the new multi-cursor test hangs instead of failing with an assertion, because the test transport has no request cap. Suggest throwing from the transport after N requests.

risk.why: Changes listItems, its tests and README in one client module. Success path unchanged except for multi-page fetching. Review rated low after the fix. npm test passes.

item.title: Add cursor pagination to GET /items
item.brief: In inventory-api, change GET /items to support optional limit (integer 1..100, default 20) and cursor (opaque string from a previous next_cursor). Return {"items": [...], "next_cursor": <string|null>}, items ordered by id, next_cursor null on the last page. Invalid limit or cursor: HTTP 400 with {"error": "..."}. Add tests covering paging, last page, invalid params and default limit. Update the README to document the new parameters and response shape. Run python3 -m unittest and make sure it passes. Commit the change. Follow the shared contract exactly.

reasons: sizer: elevated -> high; capped at medium; consider a stronger tier; unchanged

evidence.caption: Before: GET /items?limit=5 returns all 57 items, no next_cursor

pr.body: Approach: api.py list_items filters by id > decoded cursor, takes limit items, and returns next_cursor (base64 of last returned id) only when more items remain. Parsing bounds digit lengths before int() and decodes cursors strictly (base64 validate=True), so oversized or malformed input returns 400 instead of raising. Files: api.py, test_api.py, README.md. Checks: python3 -m unittest, 11 tests OK at d1ab38a. Review: whole-change reads by three reviewers failed on the oversized-digit ValueError; fixed in d1ab38a (Review-Fix trailers) and a delta review of 3f6b85e..d1ab38a passed. Assumptions: the default limit of 20 intentionally truncates GET /items for existing callers, as specified. Follow-ups (non-blocking): list_items has one assert; cursors accept non-canonical base64 and leading-zero ids; test_api.py duplicates cursor encoding; non-string query values raise AttributeError; GET /items/<5000-digit id> still raises ValueError (pre-existing in get_item); limit with more than 3 digits, including leading zeros, is now rejected.
pr.summary: GET /items now pages: limit (1..100, default 20) and cursor params; response {items, next_cursor}. Before: all 57 items, no next_cursor. Now: one page of up to 20 items plus next_cursor, null on last page; invalid limit/cursor returns 400.
pr.title: Add cursor pagination to GET /items

agt_01M89ZRR0H3WXSN3JDX2GPZ787:1.description: Oversized digit strings in limit or decoded cursor raise an uncaught ValueError (int() over 4300-digit limit) instead of returning 400 as documented; no test covers this at api.py:53

agt_01M89ZRR0H3WXSN3JDX2GPZ787:2.description: base64 decoding is lenient: urlsafe_b64decode drops non-alphabet characters, so malformed cursors such as '!!MTA=' are accepted; the cursor is opaque so this is not a documented-behaviour break, but validate=True would make it strict at api.py:64

agt_01M89ZRXW2K63E2XR2V75W3MHT:1.description: Oversized digit-only limit or cursor raises uncaught ValueError (int() over Python's 4300-digit limit) instead of returning documented 400. Verified in a temp copy: limit='1'*5000 and cursor=base64('1'*5000) both raise. Fix: validate length (e.g. reject >3 digits for limit, bounded length for cursor) or catch ValueError around int(), and add tests. at api.py:53

agt_01M89ZRXW2K63E2XR2V75W3MHT:2.description: list_items has one assert (decorative, len(page) <= limit); rules ask for at least two meaningful asserts on non-trivial functions. Consider asserting ordering/cursor invariants. at api.py:43

agt_01M89ZRXW2K63E2XR2V75W3MHT:3.description: Cursor parser is lenient: accepts non-canonical base64 (e.g. standard '+/' form such as 'Nw==') and leading-zero/'0' ids, so more than one string decodes to the same position. Harmless for correctness but weakens the 'opaque' contract; tests do not cover it. at api.py:59

agt_01M89ZRXW2K63E2XR2V75W3MHT:4.description: test_api.py duplicates the cursor encoding (cursor_after) that api._encode_cursor already implements; tests also lack a case for oversized digit input, which is how finding 1 escaped. at test_api.py:80

agt_01M89ZS3RXHCG67HF4ZM63G77X:1.description: Digit strings over 4300 characters make int() raise ValueError (Python 3.14 int-string limit), which is uncaught in the limit and cursor parsers. This is a 500-style crash instead of a 400. Reproduced with limit='1'*5000 and cursor=base64('9'*5000). Tests do not cover it. at api.py:53

agt_01M89ZS3RXHCG67HF4ZM63G77X:2.description: Same uncaught ValueError in the cursor path: int(decoded) at line 69 is outside the try block that only guards the base64/ascii decode. Cursor base64('9'*5000) crashes; cursor base64('9'*4300) returns 200 with an empty page. at api.py:69

agt_01M89ZS3RXHCG67HF4ZM63G77X:3.description: Non-string query values (for example a list) raise AttributeError. The documented contract is {str: str}, so this is out of contract and only a hardening nit. at api.py:47

agt_01M89ZS3RXHCG67HF4ZM63G77X:4.description: Behaviour change: GET /items with no parameters now returns 20 of 57 items. README documents it, and tests cover it, but existing callers that expect the full list will silently get a truncated result. at api.py:28

agt_01M89ZVVBM1KJ8GXEWAAVDT0RG:6.description: Pre-existing, outside delta: get_item calls int(raw_id) on unbounded digit strings, so GET /items/<5000 digits> raises ValueError instead of 400/404. Same class as the open oversized-digit findings. at api.py:91

agt_01M89ZVVBM1KJ8GXEWAAVDT0RG:7.description: limit with leading zeros longer than 3 chars (e.g. '0100', which equals 100) is now rejected with 400; the new 3-digit cap changes previously accepted input. at api.py:54

risk.why: api.py and README.md change GET /items behaviour: default limit 20 truncates responses for existing callers, a breaking API change for clients that expect the full list. Tests added in test_api.py. All three whole-change reviewers rated it high and the delta reviewer confirmed.
